prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: O=C(O)CCCCCCCCCCCNC(=O)NC12CC3CC(CC(C3)C1)C2
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL2409

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant human sEH using CMNPC substrate by fluoresecent-based assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of soluble epoxide hydrolase (unknown origin) using 14,15-EET as substrate incubated for 20 mins by LC-MS/MS analysis
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "NOT_COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.6, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "The two assays use different substrates (fluorescent CMNPC vs. natural 14,15-EET) and different detection methods (fluorescence vs. LC-MS/MS), which commonly yield systematically different IC50 values for sEH inhibitors due to differences in substrate affinity and assay kinetics, often exceeding 1 log unit."}

parsed.reason: The two assays use different substrates (fluorescent CMNPC vs. natural 14,15-EET) and different detection methods (fluorescence vs. LC-MS/MS), which commonly yield systematically different IC50 values for sEH inhibitors due to differences in substrate affinity and assay kinetics, often exceeding 1 log unit.
